title: `Metadata.from_email` hides an invalid `Version` when the input also has an unknown field
spec:
This is the `packaging` library (Python 3, no dependencies; the code is in `src/packaging/`). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests --ignore=tests/property` (about a minute).

```python
from packaging import metadata
metadata.Metadata.from_email(
    "Metadata-Version: 2.6\nName: packaging\n"
    "Unknown-Field: value\nVersion: invalid version\n")
```
Expected: one `ExceptionGroup` listing both problems, `unrecognized field: 'unknown-field'` and the invalid `version`.
Actual: `ExceptionGroup('unparsed', ...)` with only the unknown-field error; the bad version shows up only after that is fixed.

Please report them together in a single `ExceptionGroup` whose message is `"invalid or unparsed metadata"`, holding an `InvalidMetadata` with the right `field` for each problem, and not chained to another exception (`__context__` is `None`).

Similar inputs are probably affected too; please fix the underlying problem rather than just this case.
acceptance: the reported example produces the expected output
the underlying problem is fixed, not just the reported input
